solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Country of extreme characters awfully bare the first day of the year

parts.note: the letters at either extreme of the alphabet are A and Z

indicators.note: done awfully, the letters of 'bare' are badly jumbled into a new order

parts.note: first is the number one, written as the figure 1 and read as the letter I
Jan is the short form of January, here standing for a day such as New Year's

explanation.surface: A grumble about some nation's harsh characters, looking awful at New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns BARE into ERBA. The surface reads 'the first day of the year' as New Year's Day, 1 Jan; the figure 1 stands as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Azerbaijan is a sovereign nation in the Caucasus, so a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: Essentially unrealistic going after gold

indicators.note: the word for unrealistic is placed after the symbol for gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
fond in its older sense means foolishly credulous, holding unrealistic hopes

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be at heart a dreamer, chasing riches.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, used in English, means at bottom or basically, an idiom matching essentially.

clue.text: What comes from the heart after the finish when the finish isn't wanted

definitions.text: What comes from the heart after the finish when the finish isn't wanted

indicators.note: the word for heart comes after the shortened word for finish
the closing letter of the word for finish is not wanted, so it is dropped

parts.note: a finish is an end
the heart of something is its core

explanation.surface: A heartfelt extra performance demanded once the show is supposedly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the finish isn't wanted' drops the last letter (D) of END. Read whole, the clue also describes an extra piece demanded after a concert seems over.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat or extra item is performed after the official end of a show, at the audience's demand.

clue.text: Part of a large house in which there are lots of balls

definitions.text: Part of a large house in which there are lots of balls

parts.words: Part of a large house in which there are lots of balls
parts.note: balls suggests grand dances in a mansion, but these are the coloured spheres of a cue game kept in a dedicated games room

explanation.surface: A stately home with a ballroom seeing frequent dances.
explanation.definitionFit: A room in a country house set aside for the cue game, its table holding many balls.

clue.text: Aware of nothing in a place where one could get drunk?

indicators.note: the letter for nothing sits inside the word for a pub

parts.words: a place where one could get drunk
parts.note: an inn is a pub, where drinking happens
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone oblivious in a pub where drinking is the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To be party to a secret or plan is an idiomatic way of saying you know about it.

clue.text: Sailor, say, in the country giving up

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say goes inside the word for country

parts.note: a country is a nation
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A seaman, for example, quits life ashore in his homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-denial or renunciation: the noun names the act of renouncing something.

clue.text: Having suffered setback, go mad

indicators.note: a setback is taken as a turning back, so the word for go is read backwards

parts.note: a go at something is a stab at it

explanation.surface: After a disappointment, someone loses their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for crazy, as in having bats in the belfry.

clue.text: Old saint laid into a noodle being disloyal to the faith

indicators.note: the old saint is placed inside the word for head

parts.note: noodle is slang for the head, as is pate

explanation.surface: An elderly holy man attacks a fool for straying from religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid into' looks like an attack but is the container signal; 'noodle' is slang for the head, not pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it describes someone who has renounced their religion, a turncoat in belief.

clue.text: Tree in bottom of valley in the way of some car out of control

indicators.note: the picked letter sits obstructing the jumbled car, placed inside it
a car out of control careers about, so the letters are scrambled
the bottom of a word, in a down clue, is its last letter

explanation.surface: A tree at the foot of a valley blocking a runaway car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of control' makes the anagram SCAMORE; 'bottom of' takes the last letter of 'valley', since in a down entry the end is at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple species, a familiar example of a tree in Britain.

clue.text: Female gaining power in new location, the centre of attention

indicators.note: the jumbled word gains, taking in, the power letter
made new, the letters of location are rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A woman acquiring authority after moving somewhere becomes the star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' shuffles LOCATION into OCALOINT, and 'gaining' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally where rays converge; figuratively the thing everyone looks at.

clue.text: Necklace is light, end bit having fallen off

indicators.note: the end bit of the word for light drops off, losing its last letter

parts.note: a torch is a light

explanation.surface: A lightweight necklace whose clasp has broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like an adjective about weight; it is the noun, a hand lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a rigid twisted metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts.

clue.text: One worshipped may be seen as such — how it's formulated with prayer

definitions.text: One worshipped may be seen as such

indicators.note: a formula is worked out, so these letters are recast in a new form

explanation.surface: A deity deserves worship, as the wording of a prayer shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formulated' rearranges HOW ITS and PRAYER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything worshipped is regarded as deserving acclaim; the adjective means commendable.

clue.text: Nymph that is about to interrupt boring person

indicators.note: the turned letters break into the word for a boring person

parts.note: a nerd is a dull, obsessive person

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: that is, id est, abbreviated ie

explanation.surface: A sprite who cuts short a tedious bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the abbreviation backwards before 'to interrupt' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these are sea nymphs, daughters of Nereus.

clue.text: A plant with a bug that's eaten at university

indicators.note: the bug swallows the following letters, which go inside it

parts.note: a bug is a germ, a microbe

explanation.surface: A plant infested with a pest that gets consumed on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's eaten' is the container signal: the bug swallows 'at university'.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-growing garden annual with fluffy blue flower heads, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Offers to protect rook, one showing concern? I'd drive it away!

indicators.note: the offers surround the rook letter, shielding it

parts.note: offers at auction are bids
R is the chess notation for rook
a carer looks after and worries for someone

explanation.surface: Gestures to shelter a rook from a worried person's attempt to chase it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the device itself, with 'it' the bird; the rook in the surface is really just the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow or noisy gadget exists to frighten feathered pests off crops, so it might say this of itself.

clue.text: Brian's puzzle?

parts.note: the name Brian has its letters contorted from those of a word for the mind, so the man's name is itself a teaser of that kind

explanation.surface: A conundrum set by a man called Brian.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky riddle or teaser; jumbling the mind-organ word gives the name, which is the wit.

clue.text: Naughty?

parts.note: as plain meaning it is unseemly; read in two parts it is a real little devil, a mischief-maker in the true sense

explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly or indecent behaviour can be called naughty; split, it also suggests a genuine little devil.

clue.text: Stop and help returning male members of family

indicators.note: returning means the word for help comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: aid is help
a father, pa, is one male relative
a son is another male relative

explanation.surface: Someone asks the men of the household to quit and come back to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns AID into DIA. 'Stop' is an organ stop, not a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: On an organ the main foundation stop is named this, so an organ stop.

clue.text: Head waiter? One's tolerated him when getting into a muddle

indicators.note: words in a muddle are confused, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss puts up with an employee who keeps getting confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into a muddle' rearranges TOLERATED HIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title is used for the chief of the dining-room staff in a restaurant or hotel.

clue.text: New Testament place linked to an Old Testament place

parts.note: Cana in Galilee is where the wedding feast miracle happened

explanation.surface: A Gospel site paired with a Hebrew Bible location.
explanation.definitionFit: The promised land of the Israelites in the Hebrew scriptures, a biblical region.

clue.text: Children's game involves dance around water

indicators.note: the dance word goes around the word for water

parts.note: to bop is to dance
pee is urine, informally water as in passing water

explanation.surface: A kids' party game that includes splashing about in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' here is urine, as in passing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo-style hiding fun shares its name with the nursery-rhyme shepherdess, given as a game for little ones.

clue.text: Carpet seller, one getting along swimmingly

parts.note: a rep, sales representative, is a seller
a roach is a freshwater fish, moving by swimming

explanation.surface: A rug salesman who rubs along nicely with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb, to haul someone up for a telling-off, not a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British informal for scolding them, so a rebuke or censure.

clue.text: Loris eats a plant

indicators.note: the primate takes in the letter, which goes inside it

parts.note: the potto is a slow-moving African primate related to the loris

explanation.surface: A small primate munches on some vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber-bearing member of the nightshade family, so an example of a plant.

clue.text: Recoil from shout on the parade ground?

definitions.meaning: to avoid or keep away from something
a clipped form of the drill command 'Attention!' barked by a sergeant

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to avoid; the other is the military shortening of the word of command for standing to attention.

clue.text: To enthusiastically kiss in dance? Hard!

parts.note: pas is a ballet step, as in pas de deux
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Smooching passionately on the dance floor proves difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang, chiefly Australian and British, for snogging or necking passionately.

clue.text: Design feature of building that could feature in art archive

indicators.note: the letters of the following words could be found, arranged differently, within them

explanation.surface: A building's design element that might appear in an art collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The moulded frame around a door or window, or the beam resting on columns, is an architectural element.

clue.text: Payment coming from Greek not in regular instalments

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one, from the following words

explanation.surface: A Greek debtor failing to pay in fixed installments.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of GREEK NOT, starting from the second, is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular sum paid to a landlord for occupying property.

clue.text: Biscuit provided in bedroom before man's sleep

indicators.note: the bedroom letters come before the rest

parts.note: br is the estate agents' abbreviation for bedroom
Andy is a man's name, here with a possessive s
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A snack supplied in the bedroom ahead of someone's nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, crisp rolled ginger wafer, often cream-filled, so a type of British biscuit (a cookie).
